picks.why: A best-in-class money center at 16.2x trailing earnings, with EPS up 13.4% and the lowest volatility on the list (1.88% weekly); the steeper curve the synthesis describes helps its margins rather than hurting them.

One of the cheapest sound businesses on the table at 11.2x trailing with EPS still up 10.1%, and a disciplined underwriter whose float earns more with the 10Y at 4.745%, so its week does not depend on the jobs report or AMD.

A durable staples franchise with a long record of dividend increases, at 16.7x trailing after an 8.8% slide over 12 weeks, which is cheap for this business; it is low-volatility (2.27% weekly) and its large foreign earnings gain from the dollar falling below 100.
A profitable biotech with a large net cash position at 16.2x trailing, in the healthcare group the synthesis has on breakout watch, and tied to neither the rate trade nor the AI-chip trade.

A defense prime with a government customer at 21.5x trailing, with EPS up 52.8% as it moves past quarters hit by charges; it is already on my plant list and shielded from this week's AMD and jobs-report binaries.

summary: With the 10Y one basis point below its 52-week high and the jobs report due Friday, I bought cheap, sound businesses that don't need a particular jobs number: a bank and an insurer that do well at higher rates, a marked-down staple, a net-cash biotech and a defense prime. I avoided semis ahead of AMD on Tuesday, REITs and utilities with the 10Y near 4.75%, and commodity names whose earnings rest on near-peak prices; I also passed on the low trailing P/Es of HON and GOOGL, which may be flattered by the aerospace separation and by investment gains. I have no memory of how this week turned out, and none of this relies on one.
